title: Track-level Features
text:
Spotify Feature Overview




Most tracks cluster in the mid-to-high danceability range (0.6–0.8) with moderate energy levels.



Despite differences in genre and language, the playlist shows a clear preference for rhythmically engaging tracks with consistent groove and pacing.
Outliers correspond to perceptible mood shifts, rather than structural differences between genres.



The playlist is not genre-driven, but rhythm and energy driven.

title: Corpus & Background
text:
This corpus consists of 100+ tracks drawn from my personal Spotify listening history, spanning Dutch, English, and Spanish repertoire across rap, trap, R&B, pop, and soul.
Rather than being curated by genre, the playlist reflects long-term listening behaviour. This makes it suitable for analysing whether perceived stylistic diversity corresponds to measurable structural consistency.

title: Corpus & Background
text:
Introduction
This project analyzes a personal Spotify playlist consisting of over 100 tracks across multiple languages and genres, including rap, trap, R&B, and pop. Artists range from The Weeknd and Michael Jackson to Frenna, Coldplay, and 2Pac.
Although the playlist appears stylistically diverse, this analysis investigates whether underlying musical features reveal a more consistent structure.

title: Corpus & Background
text:
Research Question
To what extent does a stylistically diverse personal playlist exhibit underlying structural consistency in Spotify-derived audio features?

title: Corpus & Background
text:
Assumptions

Spotify audio features approximate perceptual musical qualities such as energy, mood, and rhythm

Personal listening behaviour reflects consistent preferences that can be quantified

Genre labels are less informative than feature-based representations

title: Clustering
text:
Clustering




The dendrogram reveals clear groupings of tracks based on audio features.



The playlist is not random, but structured around clusters of similar musical characteristics.
Different clusters represent variations in energy, danceability, and acousticness.



Even within a diverse playlist, tracks group together based on measurable feature similarity.



Similarity in the playlist is driven by audio features rather than genre labels.

title: Chroma Features
text:
Chromagram – Wanderlust





The chromagram shows recurring activation of specific pitch classes over time, indicating a stable tonal centre and repeated harmonic patterns.



Rather than exhibiting harmonic complexity or frequent modulation, the track relies on loop-based harmonic structures. These repeating pitch distributions align with a consistent and recognisable musical foundation.



Although the playlist appears stylistically diverse, this suggests that harmonic behaviour may be more consistent than expected across tracks.



The playlist shows harmonic consistency through stable tonal centres and repetition.

title: Contribution
text:
Although the playlist appears stylistically diverse, multiple analyses reveal consistent patterns across tracks.
These include: - stable energy levels
- consistent tempo ranges
- harmonic repetition
- similar production characteristics



This suggests that personal music taste is not primarily genre-based, but driven by deeper structural features such as rhythm, energy, and production style.




Music recommendation systems could benefit from focusing on feature similarity rather than genre labels

Personal playlists may contain hidden structure despite apparent diversity




This playlist is not a collection of different genres — it is a coherent system shaped by consistent musical preferences.

title: Loudness
text:
Correlation Matrix




Energy and loudness are strongly positively correlated (r = 0.75), while energy is negatively correlated with acousticness (r = -0.67).



Tracks in the playlist are structured around production intensity. High-energy tracks tend to be louder and less acoustic, reflecting modern production styles.



This suggests that the playlist is not only rhythmically consistent, but also consistent in its production characteristics.



The playlist favours high-energy, compressed production over acoustic variation.

title: Timbre Features
text:
Timbre SSM – Wanderlust




The self-similarity matrix shows strong temporal continuity with subtle structural segmentation.



Changes in timbre are gradual rather than abrupt. Structural transitions are driven more by layering and density than by strong timbral contrast.



This suggests that timbre is not the primary driver of variation within the playlist.



Structure is shaped more by harmonic repetition than timbral contrast.
